unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U03: Calculate bounded co-surety contribution separately from creditor enforcement

payload.title: Contribution is an internal allocation question
payload.core_explanation_md:
The creditor claim against liable sureties and the sureties contribution between themselves are different questions. Under the stated default inter-se rule, co-sureties contribute equally to the unpaid debt, subject to contrary agreement and the limits of their respective obligations. Different ceilings can require a capped allocation rather than dividing every amount equally without regard to limits.

The exercise below stipulates equal uncapped contribution and an unpaid debt amount. It does not establish the validity of a real guarantee or instruct the creditor to recover only that fraction from each person.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an equal contribution share necessarily cap the creditor independent enforcement rights?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Inter-se contribution and creditor enforcement must be distinguished.

payload.title: Allocate a stipulated uncovered balance between equal co-sureties
payload.core_explanation_md: Assume three valid co-sureties with no contrary arrangement or binding lower limits. The principal debtor has paid INR 42,000 of a covered INR 180,000 debt. Calculate each equal contribution to the remaining debt.

self_check.prompt_text: Which rule and stipulated facts determine this result?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Use the sourced rule and stated scenario assumptions; the arithmetic does not establish a live legal entitlement.

payload.stem_md: Assume four valid equally contributing co-sureties, no contrary agreement and no lower limits. A covered debt of INR 252,000 has received INR 44,000 from the principal debtor. Calculate each inter-se contribution to the remaining balance in exact INR.

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Use exact whole units; do not round intermediate values.
